title: fetchQuery
subtitle: Execute a fetch operation
description: Execute a fetch operation programmatically without React hooks. Perfect for one-time operations, event handlers, and server-side usage.

rows.name: queryKey
rows.description: Unique identifier for the query. Can be a string, array, or object.

rows.name: options
rows.description: Optional configuration object. If no fetcher is provided, uses a previously registered fetcher.

rows.name: options.fetcher
rows.description: Function that returns a Promise resolving to the data. Optional if fetcher was already registered.

rows.name: options.staleTime
rows.description: Time in milliseconds after which data is considered stale.

returns.description: Promise that resolves to the fetched data

examples.title: With Fetcher
examples.description: Execute a one-time fetch operation with inline fetcher

examples.title: Using Registered Fetcher
examples.description: Use fetchQuery with a previously registered fetcher

behavior.title: One-time Execution
behavior.description: Executes the fetch operation once and returns the result

behavior.title: Cache Integration
behavior.description: Updates the cache, affecting all components using the same query key

behavior.title: Error Handling
behavior.description: Throws errors that can be caught with try/catch

behavior.title: Promise-based
behavior.description: Returns a Promise for async/await or .then() usage

dos: Use for one-time operations like form submissions
Use in event handlers and server-side code
Combine with useQuery for reactive updates
donts: Don't use in render functions (use useQuery instead)
Don't forget to handle Promise rejections
Don't use for continuous data fetching
Don't use without proper error handling

callouts.title: Cache Integration
callouts.content: fetchQuery updates the cache, so any components using useQuery with the same key will automatically re-render with the new data.

callouts.title: Error Handling
callouts.content: Always wrap fetchQuery calls in try/catch blocks to handle potential errors gracefully.
